Thanks for running through the DPA. Attaching Helios_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf with our edits. Two asks from the legal/procurement side that we need confirmed by Product/Security before we can move to contract:

1) Subprocessors: we need a binding list for any subprocessor that will receive runtime artifacts (logs, telemetry, exported metrics). Helios requires vendor-level clarity and a right-to-approve for analytics vendors that touch runtime traces.

We are working to keep this short so procurement can sign. Can your security and product folks validate whether: (a) KV cache can be excluded from telemetry exports, and (b) whether Redwood can provide either a contractual guarantee or a runtime configuration to disable cache export?

Hannah / team — reviewed Helios' redlines and did a quick security assessment (see security-eval-notes.docx attached). Summary:

- Principle: we should avoid promises that are operationally infeasible to prove. Saying "we will never export KV cache" is risky unless we define what "export" means and how it's prevented.

- Narrow-contract approach: we can accept language that prohibits automated exports of KV cache as part of telemetry and requires explicit customer opt-in for any snapshot exports for debugging/analytics. That should satisfy Helios while staying operationally realistic.

- Runtime/technical mitigation: require encryption-at-rest for KV cache and strict ACLs for any support/debugging workflows that might access a tenant's cache. Documented access log + audit trail is a must.

- Subprocessor binding: we can provide a short-list of subprocessors that have access to telemetry artifacts and add a clause that any new analytics subprocessor requires notice and the chance for Helios to object within 30 days. That's a reasonable compromise.

Suggested contract language (brief):
"Redwood will not transmit persistent KV cache snapshots to third-party analytics providers as part of routine telemetry collection. Customer may opt-in to such snapshot exports for debugging under documented procedures; all such exports will be encrypted and logged. Redwood will maintain and provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors with access to runtime telemetry; Redwood will notify Customer of new subprocessors and Customer may object within 30 days."

If Product can build a tenant-level toggle for snapshot exports and we can ship the logging & encryption controls by the proposed timeline, I'll be comfortable recommending legal accept the compromise.

- Attachments: security-eval-notes.docx (details + risk matrix)

O
Olga Petrov

Quick product notes from runtime:

- Technical feasibility: adding a tenant-level opt-out for KV cache snapshot exports is feasible. We already tag telemetry with tenant IDs and route traces; the export path is layered (collection -> aggregator -> export). We can gate the export at the aggregator and add a boolean flag per tenant. Estimated effort: 3 engineer-weeks to implement, plus tests and a docs update. If we prioritize, we can ship a targeted mitigation (toggle + audit logging) within our July sprint.

- Compatibility impact: disabling cache exports for a tenant will reduce the fidelity of some global analytics (sampling for debugging) but will not break core inference serving. Side-effects to note: a few internal observability tools assume cache snapshot sampling; we will add fallbacks to rely on aggregate metrics instead.

- Operational guardrails: propose we ship with the following controls:
  * tenant_export_toggle (off by default)
  * mandatory encryption-at-rest for KV cache (already in place for Dedicated/private; add stronger brokered encryption for hosted)
  * export-audit-log retained 180 days (configurable)

If Legal wants a contractual guarantee, suggest the language Olga drafted but add "except as required for subpoena/compelled disclosure" carveout. Otherwise let's offer the opt-out + subprocessor notice window.

I can build a short acceptance checklist for Marissa to include in the counter-clause: implementation ETA, expected functional limits, and rollback plan.

Dev

Subject: Re: DPA edits + telem carveout request — proposed path forward

Jennifer — thanks for the redlines and patience. Internal alignment complete:

What we can commit to today (proposed counter-language):
- Redwood will not include tenant KV cache snapshots in routine telemetry exports to third-party analytics providers. Any snapshot export will be explicit, encrypted in transit and at rest, and performed only with documented customer consent.
- Redwood will provide a tenant-level configuration toggle to disable snapshot exports; we will ship the toggle and export-audit logging in July (ETA: release window week of July 20).
- Redwood will maintain and provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors with access to runtime telemetry and will notify Customer of any new analytics subprocessors; Customer may object within 30 days of notification.

Security caveat: as Olga noted, we cannot reasonably guarantee absolute prevention of compelled disclosures (subpoena), so our clause will include a standard legal exception.

Next steps I propose:
1) Helios confirms whether the above is acceptable for contract purposes (if yes, Legal will stop redlining and we can proceed to signature).
2) If Helios needs stronger language, Marissa will draft a tightened clause and we will add the implementation milestone & acceptance checklist (Dev will provide the checklist).
3) Schedule a 30-min sync next week if any of the product/security details need a quick walkthrough.

Please let me know by EOD Friday 6/25 if this path is acceptable. If so, I will ask Legal to prepare a counterproposal for Helios_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf reflecting the language above.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts
